 THIS WRIT APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 4 OF THE KARNATAKA HIGH COURT ACT PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE ORDER DATED 19/09/2022 PASSED BY THE LEARNED SINGLE JUDGE IN WP NO.10272/2020 (BDA) AND CONSEQUENTLY DISMISS THE SAID WRIT PETITION IN SO FAR AS THE APPELLANT IS CONCERNED, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.
 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
CHIEF JUSTICE DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT This intra court appeal seeks to lay a challenge to the learned Single Judge's order dated 19.09.2022 whereby private respondents' W.P.No.10272/2020 (BDA) having been favoured a Writ of Mandamus has been issued to the 3rd respondent-BDA to issue TDR and in the alternative to pay compensation for the land taken, under the provisions NC: 2023:KHC:40307-DB of Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
2.

Learned Sr. Panel Counsel appearing for the appellant-BBMP vehemently argues that the impugned order for issuance of TDR or in the alternative for payment of compensation in respect of the land utilized, could not have been made since the land is in the occupation of the appellant and that would prejudice him.
So arguing, he seeks invalidation of the impugned order.

sentences.text: 3. Learned Sr. Advocate appearing for the private respondents points out that the direction in the impugned order is to the BDA and not to the appellant; secondly, even otherwise the appellant-BBMP is not an aggrieved party inasmuch as the land in question is not ordered to be restored to the said respondents; he points out that what is ordered is only the issuance of TDR Certificate or the compensation, with which the appellant-BBMP is not concerned.
We are in full agreement with this submission and therefore decline indulgence in the appeal.
In the above circumstances, this appeal being devoid of merits is liable to be and accordingly dismissed.

Sd/-
